chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad, and Muhammad bin Yahya, from Ahmad bin Muhammad, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, from Sama'ah who said,

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'What should I say when I place one of our deceased in his grave?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Say: O Allah, this is Your servant so-and-so, and the son of Your servant, who has lodged with You, and You are the best of those with whom one lodges. He has indeed become in need of Your Mercy. O Allah, and we do not know from him except goodness, and You are more Knowing of his inner self, while we are witnesses to his outward self.'

O Allah, cause the earth to be firm away from his sides, and teach him his Proof (al-Hujjah), and make this day the best day that comes upon him, and make this grave the best house he has lodged in, and turn him into goodness from what he was in, and widen for him in his entrance, and comfort his loneliness, and forgive his sin, and do not deprive us of his reward, and do not mislead us after him.

key_terms.حُجَّتَهُ: His Proof (referring to the Imam or divine evidence he followed)
key_terms.فَجَافِ: To cause to be firm/straight (referring to the body in the grave)

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended prayer to recite when burying the dead in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi, this supplication emphasizes the dual nature of divine judgment by acknowledging the deceased's public righteousness while humbly submitting to Allah's superior knowledge of his inner secrets (sirrah). It reflects the Shia tradition of seeking intercession and comfort for the dead, asking for the grave to become a dwelling of peace rather than confinement, a theme deeply rooted in eschatological beliefs.
